rule: Loops become one-cell rectangular frames and solid blobs become single dots. Nesting is preserved with one cell of padding. Siblings are banded into rows and columns by overlapping input extents, and neighbouring 3x3 cells share their margins. A dot beside a framed sibling snaps to the unique nearest overlapping inner dot. The result is cropped to the top-level frames and dot cells.
scope: Random scenes contain one or two top-level wobbly loops plus 0-2 outside blobs. Loops hold 1-3 children in row, column, diagonal or L arrangements; children are blobs or inner loops, up to four nesting levels (the 'deep' style). Colours and grid size (up to 30) are random. The output is built from the latent tree and latent bounding boxes. Not supported: multiple foreground colours, empty loops (the reference would draw them as dots), more than 3 children per loop or more than 4 top-level objects, touching or diagonally adjacent objects, and holes inside blobs. The fixtures are replayed through the input_grid option because the hand-drawn loop shapes are impractical to parametrise; replay extracts components, enclosure and parents, then uses the same renderer. Exact width/height and outside-blob count are supported. Pair style can include two loops plus two external blobs.
constraints: Exactly one background and one foreground colour; the background is the majority colour and occupies all four grid corners.
Distinct objects are never 4- or 8-adjacent, so 4- and 8-connectivity give the same components.
Each loop is the 8-neighbour border of a notched rectangle. Its wall is 4-connected with no 2x2 wall block, and its interior is non-empty and 4-connected.
Every child keeps at least one empty cell of clearance from its parent's wall (child bbox expanded by 2 stays inside the loop region).
Blobs are corner-trimmed rectangles: 4-connected, no holes, at least 3 cells.
Every loop contains at least one child.

No sibling pair, and no leaf paired with a blob inside a sibling loop, has bounding-box projections that touch exactly (end+1 == start). This keeps inclusive and exclusive bbox conventions equivalent for banding and overlap tests.
Siblings in the same band overlap the band's widest or tallest member, so each band forms exactly one cluster and no two siblings share a (row, column) cell.
Input and output are each at most 30x30.
known_limitations: Fixture replay uses a local component/enclosure extraction from the supplied grid, not explicit latent arguments.
Rejection sampling discards scenes with projection-touching boxes, which slightly under-samples some tight packings.
Loop shapes come from rectangle notches only, so they are less irregular than the hand-drawn originals.
The layout routine reproduces the reference's banding and dot-snapping semantics, including its narrow unique-anchor snapping condition, and therefore inherits those quirks.
Bounded sampling now raises without substituting a fixed or simpler scene.
Two top-level loops with two external blobs are supported via four-root layouts; internal sibling count remains at most three.
Requested input dimensions may only pad/fit the sampled geometry; larger canvas alone is not a difficulty guarantee.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
